items.title: Microsoft shipped containers for AI agents
items.oneliner: Microsoft's MXC gives agents policy-bound sandboxes, which turns agent security from prompt hygiene into enforceable runtime controls.

items.title: Rampart redacts PII inside the browser
items.oneliner: Rampart claims 98.4% multilingual PII recall on-device, which is the privacy architecture enterprise copilots actually need.

items.title: Jane Street tested diffusion for market data
items.oneliner: Jane Street is probing autoregressive diffusion for synthetic markets, a sign generative modeling is moving into quant infrastructure.

items.title: A weak password exposed Denmark's registry
items.oneliner: An admin password of 123456 helped expose 8.8 million Danish records, proving basic IAM failures still beat exotic attacks.

items.title: Common Crawl now has blockchain timestamps
items.oneliner: Project Timestamper anchored 339 billion Common Crawl snapshots to Bitcoin, giving AI training corpora a stronger provenance trail.

items.title: Rust can now compile into readable C
items.oneliner: Eurydice turns Rust into readable C, which could unblock regulated teams stuck with C-only verification and compliance toolchains.

items.title: WSL3 looks materially faster than WSL2
items.oneliner: Independent benchmarks show WSL3 running 5% to 60% faster, making Windows a less compromised dev box for Linux workloads.

items.title: TypeSafe AI raised an enormous Series A
items.oneliner: TypeSafe AI raised $870 million at a $7.5 billion valuation, showing enterprise AI infrastructure still commands peak pricing.

items.title: A personal AI agent runs on Cloudflare
items.oneliner: Talorys runs a self-hosted personal agent on Cloudflare's free tier, pushing private AI assistants closer to commodity deployment.

items.title: Bitwarden changed its app licensing model
items.oneliner: Bitwarden is dual-licensing its apps, a reminder that open-source AI-era distribution economics are getting harder to sustain.
